report_target.purpose: Public demonstration of time-bound source-backed verification and evidence drift. This is not an endorsement, accusation, compliance opinion, or claim of exhaustive product accuracy.

research_rules: Prefer official Perplexity primary sources for product, pricing, model, and feature claims.
Preserve publication/access-time context. Do not treat an old announcement as a claim about the current product unless the wording explicitly says it remains current.
Use CONTRADICTED only when evidence directly negates the precise claim.
A source supporting its own company's statement means the source supports the claim; it does not by itself independently validate real-world performance.
Record source access time, source type, exact evidence span, and conflicting evidence before finalizing a verdict.
Do not use search snippets, LLM summaries, or secondary paraphrases as decisive evidence when a primary source exists.

candidates.claim: Perplexity Max costs $200 per month or $2,000 per year on the web app.
candidates.notes: Current official billing claim; useful clean baseline.

candidates.claim: Perplexity Enterprise Pro costs $40 per active seat per month or $400 per year.
candidates.notes: Pricing is an inherently drift-prone claim and a strong commercial monitoring example.

candidates.claim: Perplexity Enterprise Max costs $325 per active seat per month or $3,250 per year.
candidates.notes: Pair with PX-002 to show price claims that should carry explicit validity windows.

candidates.claim: As of Perplexity's Max launch announcement, Max included access to OpenAI o3-pro and Claude Opus 4.
candidates.notes: Do not call this contradicted. The correct demonstration is historical validity followed by product/model drift.

candidates.claim: Perplexity's current Max search-model roster includes GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5.
candidates.notes: Current counterpart to PX-004. Together they demonstrate why model-access claims need time-bound verification.

candidates.claim: Perplexity's current Pro and Max search-model roster includes Gemini 3.1 Pro.
candidates.notes: Model availability changes frequently; strong recurring-monitoring candidate.

candidates.claim: Perplexity says every answer in its Sales product is backed by inline citations.
candidates.notes: Treat strictly as a company assertion supported by its own page; do not infer citation correctness from citation presence.

candidates.claim: Perplexity for Sales advertises integrations through more than 400 connectors.
candidates.notes: Connector counts are highly drift-prone and commercially meaningful.

candidates.claim: Perplexity describes itself as the world's first answer engine.
candidates.notes: The source clearly shows Perplexity makes the claim, but 'world's first' is not settled merely by self-description. Candidate UNKNOWN for external-truth evaluation.

candidates.claim: Perplexity says its answer engine searches the web, identifies trusted sources, and synthesizes information into up-to-date responses.
candidates.notes: Useful methodology example because Perplexity itself advises users to double-check sources for added confidence.
